headline: SILVER FACES A TWO-CALENDAR-DAY BINARY: FOMC JULY 29 THEN PCE JULY 30 — ONE COULD LAUNCH IT, THE OTHER COULD CRUSH IT
snippet: GoldSilver.com's silver outlook for the final week of July 2026 identifies the sequential two-catalyst structure that sets up the most compressed binary in six months: the Federal Reserve's July 29 rate decision (CME FedWatch pricing a 35.8% probability of a hike at publication) followed 18 hours later by the June PCE inflation reading on July 30 — the Fed's preferred price gauge. A hold on July 29 removes the rate-hike premium that has suppressed silver since the Iran-strike oil spike, releasing physical demand at the sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces; a hike extends the compression but from a base where physical buyers demonstrably stepped in at $56.87. LBMA consensus sits at $79.57/oz for 2026, JPMorgan's base case is $81 — both imply 36-39% revaluation from the $58 handle current at publication. The PCE print on July 30 is the secondary catalyst that determines whether a hold translates into a sustained silver run or a one-day bounce: core PCE below 2.4% confirms the disinflation trajectory and locks in a September rate-cut expectation, while a hot print above 2.6% reopens the hike debate immediately after the market has priced it out. Silver investors have not seen a cleaner sequenced binary setup since the December 2024 pivot — and current positioning is significantly lighter.

headline: PHYSICAL SILVER OR SILVER MINING STOCKS? MOTLEY FOOL MAKES THE CASE FOR MINERS ON EVERY TIME HORIZON BEYOND 3 MONTHS
snippet: A Motley Fool analysis published July 25, 2026 addresses the persistent retail investor question of physical silver vs. mining equities and reaches a conclusion that challenges conventional defensive positioning: silver mining stocks and ETFs — including GDXJ — have outperformed physical bullion on every rolling time horizon beyond three months since 2023, and the outperformance accelerates as gold prices stabilize at new plateaus. GDX has returned 37.5% annualized vs. GLD's 27.7% over three years; GDXJ beat GDX by 13 percentage points in 2025 alone. The analysis argues that at $4,066 gold and $58 silver, mining equities carry forward margin expansion that physical metal cannot: every dollar of gold price appreciation above a miner's AISC flows directly to free cash flow, whereas physical ETFs capture only spot price moves. The case for physical is strongest for investors with a sub-90-day time horizon or genuine fear of counterparty risk — a subset, the author argues, that is smaller than retail positioning in SLV and PSLV implies. For junior mining investors specifically, the dual monetary + industrial demand story in silver miners is the thesis that physical ETFs structurally cannot replicate: industrial demand for solar, EV, and AI data center silver drives miner revenue independent of gold-silver ratio movements.

headline: SOLAR CAN'T ESCAPE THE COPPER-SILVER DEFICIT LOOP — LONGI'S 21 GW COPPER SWITCH JUST MOVES THE CRISIS, NOT SOLVES IT
snippet: A July 2026 Benzinga analysis examines the downstream consequence of Longi Green Energy's announced switch from silver to copper paste in its 21 GW solar panel manufacturing line — a move framed as a silver demand reduction that several analysts have interpreted as a structural negative for silver. The piece argues the substitution solves nothing: it transfers solar demand from silver (currently in its sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces) to copper (LME inventories down 28% since May, SHFE stocks collapsed 82%, Yangshan premium at $103-109/tonne — the highest since December 2023). Solar silver demand is forecast to decline 19% to approximately 151 million ounces in 2026, but the Silver Institute's supply-demand model shows the deficit persists because industrial demand from AI data center wiring and EV battery contact points absorbs the freed ounces immediately. On the copper side, Longi's 21 GW conversion — approximately 140,000 tonnes of incremental copper demand at current metallization ratios — arrives into the tightest LME inventory environment since 2021. Both metals remain structurally constrained regardless of which one solar manufacturers prefer at any given moment: the deficit loop cannot be escaped by moving between two simultaneously depleted commodities.

headline: KINROSS ALSO REPORTS JULY 29: $0.67 EPS AND $2.24B REVENUE EXPECTED — SCOTIABANK CUTS ESTIMATES BUT STOCK HAS BEATEN CONSENSUS 4 QUARTERS RUNNING (NYSE: KGC)
snippet: Kinross Gold (NYSE: KGC; TSX: K) reports Q2 2026 earnings after market close on July 29 — the same session as the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision and Agnico Eagle's Q2 results, creating a triple event for gold equity investors. Analyst consensus sits at $0.67 EPS and $2.24 billion in revenue, derived primarily from the La Coipa and Manh Choh mines and supported by sustained production from Round Mountain and Bald Mountain. Scotiabank cut its Q2 estimates in a July 21 note, citing higher-than-expected fuel and labour costs at Alaskan operations — a concern that recurred in Q1 but did not prevent an EPS beat. Kinross has beaten consensus EPS in four consecutive quarters, and the Buy consensus price target of C$30 implies approximately 18% upside from current levels. At $4,051/oz gold realized in Q2 vs. a guidance-implied AISC of approximately $1,300-1,350/oz, Kinross's margin profile should be among the widest reported in its history if fuel cost headwinds are contained. The July 29 triple event — rate decision, Agnico results, Kinross results — makes it potentially the most information-dense afternoon for gold equities since Newmont's Newcrest integration quarter.

headline: GLADIATOR METALS DRILLS 32m AT 1.36% Cu AT CUB EAST — YUKON COPPER STRIKE NOW 300m+ WITH 50,000m PROGRAM RUNNING (TSXV: GLAD)
source_name: North of 60 Mining News / Gladiator Metals
snippet: Gladiator Metals Corp. (TSXV: GLAD) released assay results from the Cub East Zone at its Whitehorse Copper Project in Yukon, reporting hole BCG-035 returned 32 metres at 1.36% copper, 0.63 g/t gold, and 10.93 g/t silver from 178 metres depth — including a higher-grade interval of 18 metres at 2.12% copper, 1.06 g/t gold, and 15.7 g/t silver. Companion hole BCG-024 returned 32.7 metres at 1.06% copper. The new results extend the Cub East strike to over 300 metres and confirm the zone is open along strike and at depth. The company's 50,000-metre 2026 drill program — among the most aggressive programs at an active Yukon copper discovery — is designed to define a resource at Cub East, Cub, and WCP South simultaneously. The project is located approximately 15 kilometres south of Whitehorse with existing road access and proximity to the Pacific Coast, which meaningfully reduces the infrastructure-build risk that hampers most Yukon copper discoveries. At $6.55/lb copper on Comex and less than 2% from the US all-time record, a 1.36% copper drill hole from 178 metres in a 300m+ confirmed zone in a tier-1 Canadian jurisdiction and first-class infrastructure corridor represents one of the more compelling economic discovery metrics available in the junior copper space.

headline: MCFARLANE LAKE EXTENDS JUBY GOLD STRIKE 2.5X TO 1.9KM — 179m AT 0.87 g/t Au CONFIRMS OPEN-PIT SCALE IN ONTARIO TIMMINS CAMP
snippet: McFarlane Lake Mining Limited released July 23, 2026 drill results from the Juby Gold Project west of Gowganda, Ontario — on the northwest margin of the Timmins Gold Camp — reporting two landmark intercepts: 179 metres at 0.87 g/t gold, and 155 metres at 0.90 g/t gold. The results extend the confirmed mineralized strike from 0.75 kilometres to 1.9 kilometres — a 2.5-fold increase in a single drill program — and represent the widest consistent gold intercepts yet reported at Juby. The geometry — wide, shallow-dipping, surface-accessible intervals — is the hallmark of economically viable bulk-tonnage open-pit gold mining, where lower cutoff grades are compensated by high-volume throughput and low strip ratios. Located in Ontario's Timmins Gold Camp, one of the most productive and infrastructure-rich gold-mining jurisdictions in Canada, Juby's expanding footprint at $4,066/oz gold positions it as a potential economic open-pit development target requiring a preliminary economic assessment to define the scale threshold. The 2.5× strike extension is a non-linear re-rating event for a junior gold explorer: it moves Juby from a localized discovery into a district-scale system requiring re-evaluation of the entire project footprint.

headline: INTEGRA FLORIDA CANYON: RECORD Q2 MINING RATES, GOLD UP 30% QoQ — NEW FEASIBILITY STUDY ADDS 74% MORE RESERVES (TSXV: ITR)
snippet: Integra Resources Corp. (NYSE American: ITRG; TSXV: ITR) reported July 23, 2026 that its Florida Canyon Mine in Nevada produced 16,379 attributable gold ounces in Q2 2026 — a 30% quarter-over-quarter increase — at a record mining rate of 87,867 tonnes per day, alongside a 47% increase in heap leach ore placement versus Q1. The company simultaneously released an updated feasibility study that adds 74% to proven and probable reserves, extending the mine life to eight years on a significantly larger reserve base than the prior study supported. Full-year 2026 production guidance of 70,000-75,000 ounces is maintained. Florida Canyon's operational profile — a Nevada heap leach operation with proven metallurgy, existing federal permits, and no indigenous land claims — makes its feasibility study reserve expansion one of the most direct resource-to-cash-flow conversions available in the junior gold producer space at $4,066/oz gold. A 74% reserve addition at a producing mine in a Tier 1 U.S. jurisdiction — where new mine permitting timelines average 10-15 years — is the kind of result that typically closes the valuation gap between development-stage NAV and producer multiples.

headline: CHINA CONTROLS THE CRITICAL MINERALS CHESSBOARD AS TRUMP RAISES STAKES — HOW THE DUAL-FRONT POLICY WAR IS BIFURCATING REE SUPPLY CHAINS
snippet: An InvestorNews critical minerals report published July 22, 2026 analyzes the dual-front policy conflict now structurally bifurcating rare earth element supply chains: China's MOFCOM June 22 addition of MP Materials and USA Rare Earth — the two leading U.S. rare earth producers — to its export control list, prohibiting supply of China-origin feedstocks; and the Trump administration's January 2026 Section 232 proclamation on processed critical minerals, imposing tariffs designed to incentivize domestic refining investment. The report identifies the resulting gap: China controls approximately 90% of global rare earth processing capacity, and the MOFCOM additions mean the two Western companies most capable of scaling alternative production are now cut off from the Chinese feedstock that underpins their current processing economics. The EU's €3 billion emergency critical minerals task force and Energy Fuels' US$1.9 billion acquisition of Astron Corporation's Donald Rare Earth Project in Australia represent the Western response — but both operate on 5-10 year timelines to meaningful capacity. With germanium up 27.8% and dysprosium up 25.4% in July alone (NdPr hitting ¥747-767/kg, a 2026 high), the window for Western-jurisdiction junior REE explorers with established resources and existing infrastructure is narrowing toward the point where institutional capital must commit before ex-China supply becomes demonstrably inadequate.
